name: Interdisciplinary Arts (Min)

rules.name: Narrative Text
rules.desc:
To earn a Minor in Interdisciplinary Arts, students must complete at least 27 units of coursework in the program and a senior capstone project. Required coursework includes a foundational class in interdisciplinary methods, an experiential arts course, and 13-15 units of electives that focus on the intersection of two or more disciplines. The minor culminates in an interdisciplinary capstone over the senior year and is supported by a faculty advisor and an accompanying series of workshops.
All core and elective courses should be completed prior to commencing the capstone sequence (ARTSINST 200A, B and C) in senior year. Petitions to complete some elective and/or core courses concurrently with the senior workshop sequence may be approved if the study plan presents adequately robust preparation. However, no minor requirements may be completed after the workshop sequence (e.g. during a co-term year after completion of the workshop sequence).
Students must declare the minor in Axess no later than the Final Study List Deadline of the autumn quarter of their senior year, although they are encouraged to declare sooner. Students are invited to discuss the minor with the Stanford Arts Institute’s Associate Director and prepare a Plan of Study that includes the focus of the minor study and a list of elective courses planned to fulfill the requirements. Students must also complete a Capstone Proposal in the spring quarter of their junior year. The Faculty Director must approve the Study Plan and Capstone Proposal.

Inter-Arts Minor and Honors in the Arts
If a declared Inter-Arts Minor is accepted to Honors in the Arts, they have two choices:
A) the student may drop the minor and declare Honors in the Arts (IHN) instead, or
B) the student may pursue both the Inter-Arts Minor and Honors in the Arts, but must also complete 6 additional units of coursework, to be approved by the Faculty Director, in order to satisfy the requirements of both programs.
In senior year, any Inter-Arts Minors who have been accepted to Honors in the Arts will enroll in the Honors Capstone Workshop series (ARTSINST 201A, B, & C) for up to five units per quarter. For those students completing both the Inter-Arts Minor and Honors in the Arts, this workshop series replaces the Interdisciplinary Arts Capstone Workshop series (ARTSINST 200A, B & C).

blocks.name: Core Program Requirements

rules.name: Foundational Course
rules.desc:
The foundation requirement (3-4 units) allows students to engage with the theory and/or practice of interdisciplinary art. Courses that meet this requirement will A) build students' competence and curiosity across an array of art forms and mediums through analysis and/or creative practice; B) investigate art-making as a means of exploring and responding to non-art disciplines; and/or C) explore the intersection and multidirectional impact of new technologies and creative practice.

rules.name: Interdisciplinary Arts Electives
rules.desc:
13-15 units. The remaining 13-15 units of the 27-unit minor must be satisfied by elective courses from at least two departments that encourage the interdisciplinary/intermedia ambition of the minor. To declare the minor, students must develop a coherent study plan of electives, focusing on one or two disciplinary intersections, so that the student is well-prepared to complete an interdisciplinary creative capstone in their senior year. All electives must be approved by the Faculty Director.
A subset of the 2-unit courses offered as part of Arts Intensives / Sophomore College are pre-approved as electives for the Inter-Arts Minor:

• TAPS 24AX Beyond the Garment: A Wearable Art Exploration

• EDUC 15SC: Remix | Writing and Reading the DJ

• CHEMENG 12SC: An exploration of Art Materials: The Intersection of Art and Science

All electives must be approved by the Faculty Director. In general, electives should be taken for a letter grade, but exceptions may be granted. Please contact artsinstitute@stanford.edu for any questions.

blocks.notes: Students are encouraged to develop a coherent plan for their coursework. A successful program of study will focus on one or two disciplinary intersections so that the student is well-prepared to complete an interdisciplinary creative capstone in their senior year.

rules.name: Capstone Proposal
rules.desc: Students must also complete a Capstone Proposal in Spring Quarter of their junior year. Both the Study Plan and Capstone Proposal must receive approval by the Faculty Director.

rules.name: Capstone Courses
rules.desc: Complete either option A or option B below.

children.name: A. Inter-Arts Capstone Project
children.desc: Students may design an inter-arts capstone project to be completed within the senior workshop series (ARTSINST 200A, B & C) for two units per quarter, for a total of 6 units.

children.name: B. Honors in the Arts
6 additional units approved by the faculty director, when you also receive Honors in the Arts

children.desc: Students may apply to complete an Honors in the Arts creative thesis within the senior honors workshop series (ARTSINST 201A, B & C) for a minimum of two units per quarter. Students who pursue this option and wish to receive the IHN "Honors in the Arts" in addition to the Inter-Arts Minor degree must also complete 6 additional units of coursework, to be approved by the faculty director. Please consult with the SAI Associate Director for more information.

grading: Courses used to satisfy all units taken for the minor must be taken for a letter grade, though the faculty director may grant exceptions in extenuating circumstances.
policies:
• Units from courses taken from other departments or programs within Stanford may count for major/minor requirements, with the approval of the faculty director.

• Students may not count courses for both a major and a minor.
reviewNotes: Every course must be taken for a letter grade unless the faculty director grants an exception, toward the 27 units the minor needs. The audit checks the foundational course, 3 units of experiential inter-arts courses (ARTSINST 12AX needs 20AX to reach them), and the capstone: ARTSINST 200A-C for 6 units, or ARTSINST 201A-C for at least two units each. On the 201 option, receiving Honors in the Arts as well takes 6 more units the faculty director approves. The capstone courses do not also count as electives. You move in the 13 units of electives the faculty director approves (from at least two departments) and check the capstone proposal by hand.
